holidays.name: Pardon Day
holidays.description: A day for forgiving, letting grudges go, and wiping the slate clean. You can forgive a friend, a sibling, or the coworker who microwaved fish in the break room.
holidays.origin: It marks September 8, 1974. On that day President Gerald Ford granted Richard Nixon a full pardon for any offenses he may have committed while in office, a month after Nixon resigned.
holidays.funFact: Ford announced the pardon in a televised address on a Sunday morning. It was so controversial that many historians think it hurt his 1976 election campaign.

holidays.name: Star Trek Day
holidays.description: Fans of the sci-fi franchise celebrate with marathons, Vulcan salutes, and a lot of "Make it so" and "Engage." Wearing a Starfleet uniform to work is optional but encouraged.
holidays.origin: The first episode of Star Trek, "The Man Trap," aired on NBC on September 8, 1966. Fans have honored the date as the franchise's birthday ever since.
holidays.funFact: The original series was canceled after three seasons because of low ratings. Reruns later made it a global phenomenon.

holidays.name: National Iguana Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the spiky, sun-loving lizards, from the green iguanas in pet shops to the wild ones that sunbathe on tropical rooftops. It also reminds people that iguanas are demanding pets that need serious care.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that aims to teach people about iguana conservation and responsible ownership. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Iguanas have a light-sensing "third eye" on top of their heads, called the parietal eye. It helps them detect shadows from predators overhead.
